key_insight: Risk-seeking optimization for bosonic state preparation shifts focus from average fidelity to the high-fidelity tail of the prepared-state distribution, enabling much better best-case states under noise.
engineering_relevance: For quantum engineering, this offers a tunable way to choose between higher average performance and a higher probability of producing usable encoded states on noisy bosonic hardware.
method: Adapt risk-sensitive objective functions from reinforcement learning to quantum state preparation.
Optimize a variational ansatz over stochastic photon-loss outcomes while emphasizing selected high-fidelity samples.
Adjust the objective to trade off success probability against the lowest infidelity threshold reached.
evidence_signal: Across the evaluated experimental settings, risk-seeking objectives reduced infidelities for some pure states by up to four orders of magnitude versus standard average-fidelity optimization.
watch_item: The method improves a subset of outcomes by sacrificing average fidelity, so it must be matched carefully to applications that can tolerate lower ensemble-average performance.
paper_title: Steering the Fidelity in State Preparation on Noisy Bosonic Systems with Risk-Seeking Optimization
